summary: A word-sized trend line: one stroke through every value of a float array, scaled from its min to its max to fill the canvas, with a dot on the latest value.

values.doc: A float array, "@name" of resources.floatArrays (export it to let the host replace the series); 2 or more values, any range: the line spans min..max

color.doc: Line and dot colour (onSurface in mono)

fill.doc: Fill the space the caller gives it (fillMaxSize) instead of width × height; give it a parent with a size or a weight

showDot.doc: Mark the last value with a 3 dp dot

pitfalls: values is the name of a float array ("@visits" declared in resources.floatArrays), not a JSON list: the chart reads it with arrayGet in a loop, so a host that sets the exported array redraws it with no new document, and any length works
The line is a loop of drawLine segments (round caps hide the joins), not an SVG path: a path string costs about 4 KB in Java

The y range is the data's own min..max, so a flat series sits on the bottom edge and small changes look large; that is what a sparkline is for, but don't put one next to a bar chart and expect the same scale
Everything scales with componentWidth() and componentHeight(), read inline in each coordinate; it keeps the call out of pattern mode, which is fine for a chart drawn once or twice
